items.headline: Yen shines as AI jitters spur safe-haven rush: USD/JPY ~156.28 (yen's strongest in 1+ months), DXY 101.52, 10Y 4.953% — Nasdaq -2.6% (worst since June) on AI-capex doubts (Meta -7%, AMD -8%, Nvidia -4%); no dollar haven bid
Japan Sep core CPI 2.1% y/y inline — first print above BoJ's 2% target in nine months; core-core 2.4% (from 1.9%), services 1.5% (from 1.2%) — cements the near-term (December ~80%) hike case
UK GfK consumer confidence collapsed to -24 (vs -14 fcst) — biggest monthly drop since Apr 2020; inflation expectations at the highest since April

Aramco told staff to evacuate Dhahran HQ (first since the Iran war began) as Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure intensified — Brent settled $113.17 (+4.0%, highest since May 4), pushed above $114 in Asia

French debt risk premium reaches euro-zone sovereign crisis levels: OAT-Bund 173.58bp (widest since Nov 2011); 10Y OAT tested 5.14%; Macron banned Saturday's Lyon protests, deployed troops; Moody's reviews France Friday (Aa3 neg → A1 expected)

Oil little changed overnight (Brent ~$113, WTI ~$98-99) as supply concern lingers; Gulf markets fell (TASI -1.2%) on fresh Houthi strikes; NYT: US/Israel drew up specific plans for renewed Iran strikes after the Nov-3 midterms; US ordered diplomats out of Saudi Arabia
EZ consumer confidence -17.9 in October (vs -17.0 fcst; Sept rev. to -16.8) — second straight monthly fall as high energy costs keep households pessimistic
AU flash PMIs a big miss: composite 47.7, services 47.8, manufacturing 49.7 (first private-sector contraction in 5 months); input-cost inflation fastest since May
Japan flash PMIs: manufacturing 53.3 (7-month low, miss vs 54.5 fcst), services 52.0 up from 51.3, composite 52.3 (19th month of expansion)
CME FedWatch (Oct 23): Oct 27-28 hold ~93% (~7% hike odds, down from ~16% Oct 21); December hike ~90% — Warsh corralled the October pause
RBNZ Oct-28 hike ~98% (Reuters; swaps ~85%); terminal 3.25-3.50% (ING); NZD near 0.5700 on the prospects — 100% chance of 50bp before end-Feb
Gold ~$4,013-4,022 (-2.5% to -3%) — near the 3-month low despite risk-off; cross-market liquidation in the equity rout; silver -4.8%
RBA Nov-3 hike ~44-50% (LSEG ~42% Oct 21; Hauser: ~50% Oct 20 — 'inflation outlook worse'); December ~64%; Q3 CPI Oct 28 the pivot
10Y -19bp to 4.956% (biggest one-day drop since Mar 2023) as investors fled to bonds; 2Y 4.659% — dollar pressured by lower yields
US jobless claims 194K (vs 200K fcst; -6K; near 57-year lows); continuing claims 1.728M (+25K). Fed funds futures cut Oct-28 hike odds to ~11% (from ~13%)
Canada IPPI +2.0% m/m beat (vs 0.7% fcst; +14.5% y/y, 24th straight annual gain); RMPI +4.8% beat (vs 0.1%; +27.0% y/y) — upstream heat 6 days before the Oct-28 BoC
CBI Oct industrial order expectations -32 miss (vs -20 fcst, from -9); UK factory gloom deepens, output outlook steadies — GBP held near 1-month high on the CPI-driven BoE path
China FDI -4.3% y/y Jan-Sep (548.8B yuan, $82.2B) — decline narrowed from -5.3%; high-tech +33.8%
SNB September-discussions summary (released Oct 22): franc's carry-trade appeal acknowledged (widening rate differentials, low volatility); FX intervention readiness eased — tolerates franc weakness
BoJ Dec hike ~80% (Japan Times/Bloomberg, Oct 21, via ex-BoJ exec Maeda); Oct 29-30 hold ~88-90%; national core CPI tonight 18:30 CT (2.1% fcst)
UK Sep CPI verified: 3.5% y/y beat (vs 3.4% fcst; highest since Oct 2025 on energy; core 2.8%; services 3.7% sticky) — locks BoE Nov-5 hike; GBP near 1-m high, 17-mth high vs EUR
NZ Q3 CPI 0.7% q/q, 3.7% y/y — soft miss vs 0.8%/3.8% fcst (below RBNZ 3.9% proj; sector-factor core 2.8%) — hike stayed ~98% priced
